sources.title: Effect of L-carnitine on exercise performance in patients with mitochondrial myopathy
sources.citation: Brazilian Journal of Medical and Biological Research2015;48(4):354–362
sources.depth: Complete scientific main plus all six native table images and native flowchart; no individual-data reanalysis.

model.population: Biopsy-confirmed mitochondrial myopathy with CPEO, exercise intolerance/mild weakness/myalgia
model.healthy_reference_scope: Untreated; baseline testing only; no constant-work endurance test
model.excluded: Severe limb weakness, renal/cardiac/pulmonary dysfunction, concomitant ergogenic supplements, regular physical activity in preceding year

intervention.chemical_synonym: levocarnitine, verified separately by official nomenclature
intervention.route: oral capsule once daily with breakfast or lunch
intervention.design: Randomized double-blind crossover;6participants per initial sequence
intervention.randomization_and_allocation_details: Random assignment reported; reproducible sequence/concealment details not supplied
intervention.adherence: Authors report100% adherence and no dropouts; weekly telephone/monthly visits and empty bottles, not biochemical verification

outcomes.endpoint: Constant-work cycling time to limit of tolerance
outcomes.scope: Actual endurance function at70%ofpeak workload; identical absolute load across visits not established

outcomes.limit: Pulmonary volume, not clinical respiratory benefit or muscle-force restoration

outcomes.significance: No significant marker; do not silently repair printed values or claim a lower ratio here

outcomes.endpoint: Peak incremental exercise variables including oxygen uptake,work rate,lactate and symptoms
outcomes.direction: No significant intervention differences reported in Results/Table5
No significant intervention differences reported in Results/Table4

analysis_limits: Methods describes repeated-measures crossover model for treatment/carryover, but native Tables4–6 say unpaired t-test. Actual model-derived contrast cannot be independently reconstructed.
No sequence,period or carryover estimates; a four-week washout alone does not establish no carryover.
No exact P values or confidence intervals for positives; no multiplicity correction or prospectively verified endpoint hierarchy identified.
Endurance is called the principal variable in post hoc power analysis; post hoc power does not establish prospective adequacy.
CWR specified as70%ofpeak; identical absolute workloads across visits were not demonstrated.
source_issues: Discussion says significant body-composition change, contrary to Results/Table4 and its subsequent context. Retain measured null rather than silently inserting a missing word.
Mean/SD age differs between abstract and Table1; actual age range unavailable.
Native Table6 exhaustion GER is numerically higher and unmarked; preserve isotime-specific lower GER only.
sources.mechanism_limit: Observed exercise intolerance and physiological treatment response do not prove measured carnitine deficiency, restored muscle carnitine, substrate flux, mitochondrial repair, BUB1B engagement or genotype rescue.
sources.safety_scope: Side effects were solicited; no detailed adverse-event table or renal-safety analysis supplied. No dropouts/adherence is not proof of no harm.

sources.title: L-carnitine supplementation in Duchenne muscular dystrophy steroid-naïve patients: a pilot study
sources.depth: Complete original abstract mirrored by institution and corroborated at author-upload landing page; no main/table/figure/supplement reading.
sources.design_as_abstract: Double-blind controlled trial;20patients assigned to L-carnitine or placebo
sources.model: Steroid-naïve DMD; no participant-level deficiency test verified at this depth
sources.dose: 50mg/kg twice daily as printed, not assumed50mg/kg total per day
sources.analysis: Evaluations every four months; ANOVA as reported
sources.outcome: No between-group clinical benefit in upper/lower-extremity function,P>.05
sources.safety: Abstract reports tolerability and no significant side effects; detailed event/renal assessments unverified
sources.access_limit: Author-PDF indexed as6pages, but ordinary direct download403 and screenshots timeout/no inspectable image. No native PDF cached/hash/full-read credit.
sources.notice_limit: No verified PMID/DOI in bounded searches; no linked notice identified, with limited coverage.

gene_search_scope.limit: Lexical screen, not86complete readings and not global absence proof. Endogenous/acylcarnitine/enzyme/reference co-occurrence is not treatment efficacy.

deferred_primary_leads.scope: Search excerpt only; not one of the two qualified studies
deferred_primary_leads.question: Separate L-carnitine-tartrate monotherapy leg-strength result from composite-endpoint null and multicomponent creatine/leucine/vitaminD preparation; no inherited efficacy here.

deferred_primary_leads.scope: Original metadata and publicly displayed primary excerpts encountered; main not qualified
deferred_primary_leads.question: Determine whether monotherapy cytoskeleton protection is only morphology or includes chromosome-number fidelity; do not infer aneuploidy rescue.
L-carnitine plus omega3 is a combination, not isolated L-carnitine efficacy.
L-carnitine plus acetyl-L-carnitine plus cinnoxicam cannot establish isolated L-carnitine chromosome rescue.

recommended_disposition.decision: Retain a substantive controlled human endurance reserve, with explicit small-study/statistical/access limits and DMD functional counterevidence.
recommended_disposition.niacin_comparison: Actual controlled endurance is empirical functional evidence; niacin retains separate human NAD engagement and restoration hypothesis. Neither has MVA rescue established.
recommended_disposition.apitegromab_comparison: Does not replace the stronger randomized disease-specific motor-function comparison on this small CPEO study; MVA transfer is unproved for both.
recommended_disposition.creatine_comparison: Creatine has separate selected DMD-strength positives and functional nulls; no head-to-head superiority inferred.
